text:
amy: Hey team — customer reported a sudden drop in embeddings throughput this morning after a deploy. They were seeing ~150k vectors/sec steady, now down to ~40k. No errors in the app, just timeouts and backlog. Ticket #4529 opened.
ingrid: Thx @amy. Do we know if this is vectors/sec (embedding output) vs tokens/sec (text gen)? Some folks mix those metrics. Can you paste the metrics you have? :ear:
mike: Adding infra traces. On the node hosting the embedding model pool we see GPU util at ~95% but worker queue depth is spiking to 250+ for short bursts.amy: From customer logs: "vectors/sec": 42k, "p95_latency_ms": 1200, "requests_per_sec": 18. Previously vectors/sec correlated with requests/sec * vectors_per_request. They use batch size of 128 on client.raj: Can you share the model and config? Might be a dimension mismatch push or changed default batching window.amy: Model: open_embedding_v2 (3072-d). Config on their Dedicated: batch_size=128, max_concurrency=64, batching_window_ms=30, quantized=false.ingrid: 3072-d is expected. But if client switched to sending 4096 dims accidentally we'd drop to CPU fallback or fail — any dimension mismatch errors in logs? amy: No dimension errors logged. Just slow processing and some 504s.thao: I pulled the serving logs for the pool. I see a spike in batch sizes hitting 256+ due to a bug in batching logic for certain request shapes. Batches larger than the calibration profile cause per-token throughput to degrade nonlinearly.gpu-monitor: GPU node snapshot @ 2026-03-15T09:12:22Z:
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv
utilization.gpu [%], utilization.memory [%], temperature.gpu [C]
95, 78, 82

Processes:
python (pid 2342) --gpu-memory 35GB
python (pid 2399) --gpu-memory 34GB

Queue depth (serving runtime): 260
Avg batch size: 218
Avg latency per-token: 0.012ms

mike: That avg batch size is the smoking gun. Our kernels were tuned up to batch 192 for that model. Above that, kernel launch overhead + memory thrash kills perf.ingrid: Agreed. It also explains why vectors/sec dropped: with huge batches we saturate memory copies and stall GPU pipelines. Need to cap max_batch_size and adjust batching window.amy: Customer is on Dedicated; can we hotfix by patching batching max to 192? And maybe enable backpressure so client requests get 429 rather than piling up.raj: Proposed quick mitigation steps:
1) Patch serving config: max_batch_size=192, batching_window_ms=25.
2) Set pool.max_inflight_requests=120 to limit concurrency.
3) Add temporary rate-limit rule for that customer to 80 rps.
4) Rollout canary to 1 node then widen.thao: I can push the config change to the cluster now. Rolling to 1/6 nodes in the pool. Monitoring hooks active.mike: While rolling, add a kernel telemetry snapshot to watch for OOM and queue depth. Also check if quantized variant improves throughput without quality regressions.ingrid: For long-term: we should update model profiles to include a sharp perf cliff above calibrated batch sizes; also add a hard cap in runtime and a soft backoff to prevent these artifactual spikes. I'll file an infra/serving PR.amy: Customer update: I told them we're investigating and applying temporary rate limits + config changes. They asked for repro steps they can run while we patch.raj: Repro steps for support/eng to validate the issue locally:
1) Spin up local dedicated replica: MODEL=open_embedding_v2 DIM=3072
2) Run this load generator (Python):
```
# loadgen.py (simplified)
import requests, time
url = 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings'
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer <key>'}
def batch_payload(size):
    return {'input': ['x'*128]*size, 'dimension': 3072}

for b in [64,128,192,256,320]:
    t0 = time.time()
    r = requests.post(url, json=batch_payload(b), headers=headers, timeout=30)
    dt = time.time()-t0
    print(b, r.status_code, 'latency', dt)
```
Run it with increasing interleaved concurrency to reproduce queue buildup.thao: In our canary roll I already saw p95 drop from 1200ms -> 180ms after capping max_batch_size to 192 and reducing inflight requests. vectors/sec recovered to ~140k on that node.amy: Nice. Any side effects? Did we see increased request rejection? thay: We saw a small bump in 429s while clients adjusted. Customer traffic smoothed out after their client decreased their batch_size from 128 to 64 for a patch window.ingrid: Note for docs: recommend client-side max_batch <= model_profile.max_batch and exponential backoff. Also clarify dimensions must match; add clearer error for dim mismatch instead of silent CPU fallback.mike: For billing and support, track any failed requests and issue credits if their SLA was impacted. Support team, tag the ticket for credits review.amy: I'll keep ticket owner and send a postmortem once we stabilize. Thanks everyone for quick triage. :rocket:
thao: Follow-up: opened GH issue infra#987 - "batching cliff for embeddings models" with proposed fixes (hard caps, telemetry). ingrid will own perf profile updates.ingrid: I'll add a regression test to our eval harness to run extreme batch sizes and ensure we alert when avg_batch_size>profile.max*1.1.amy: Closing loop with customer now. I'll post final status in ticket and thread when done.raj: Final note — consider adding a realtime control plane metric: per-pool avg_batch_size and kernel_efficiency, so ops can autopatch throttles before user-visible degradation.amy: Agreed. Marking this resolved for now; re-open if anything recurs. :white_check_mark:
